_comment: Pertinence verdicts, keyed by a digest of the text itself so the same sentence is judged once wherever it appears. Written by ETL/terms/classify_eligibility_pertinence.py; read by website/frontend/scripts/check_gate_pertinence.ts, which FAILS THE BUILD on a filter gate whose current text has no verdict here. Do not hand-edit a verdict: correct the text, or record the case in data/reference/gate_role_overrides.json where the reasoning lives.
_property: A published eligibility text is shown to a founder under the heading "who may apply". Judge what KIND of statement it is, AS A WHOLE, in whatever language it is written.    condition    -- a requirement about the applicant: who may apply, what the project must be, what is excluded, what thresholds apply. A reader can check it against their own company, project or plans. It stays a condition when it is narrow, hard to meet, or stated in the past tense about how the scheme has operated.                   A condition DISCRIMINATES: it is true of some readers and false of others. A requirement stated as a list of NAMED parties -- particular companies, named centres, an enumerated set of beneficiaries -- is not a condition however checkable the list looks, because no reader can come to be one of them and the answer is therefore the same for everyone. Being told to check whether you are on a closed list is not a test you can pass. Those are reports.    demand_match -- a fact about what the instrument OFFERS, of a kind an applicant is separately asked to state their own counterpart for: how much money it provides, in what form (grant, loan, equity, guarantee), to what kind of counterparty it provides it, what share of costs it covers, what maturity of company it backs. It says nothing about the applicant's merit, but an applicant who has said what they are looking for can be compared against it and the comparison means something to them -- someone seeking EUR 20 million is genuinely not served by a EUR 250,000 micro-loan.    report       -- a decision, finding or narrative about aid already allocated to parties the document names; a compatibility or selectivity conclusion; an administrative, procedural, legal-basis or budgetary fact about the scheme; a duty that binds a beneficiary only after an award; a fragment or section heading stating no requirement. There is nothing in it the reader could clear and nothing in it for them to want.  The line between demand_match and report is whether the statement is about the SHAPE OF THE OFFER, which an applicant has a preference about, or about the SCHEME'S ADMINISTRATION and decisions already taken, which they do not. A total programme budget, a disbursement calendar, an aid legal basis and a list of chosen beneficiaries are all reports even though they are facts about the money. Mentioning something an applicant is asked about -- a country, a sector, a date -- does not make a finding into a demand_match: if the statement records a decision already taken about named others, it is a report.  If a text mixes kinds and a founder could still act on part of it, prefer "condition". Answer "report" only when there is nothing to act on and nothing to want.
_versions: Each verdict carries `v`, the property version it was judged under; absent means 1. REJUDGE in the classifier declares which of an old version's answers the current property could move, and the check fails on any that are still carried at a stale version. Without this a reworded property would keep answering with verdicts nobody asked for, and the build would be green on them.
